What the gate exists for is the DECLARATION: the form is covered by an email-OTP modal (#emailVerify plus a .modal-backdrop) that must be cleared before any control is interactive, and clearing it needs a real inbox, so it is the applicant's own step and is declared as an otp handoff rather than replayed. The two blocked gate controls, for the handoff node: 'Continue' = #emailVerify button[onclick=\"VerifyEmail()\"] (1 match; the button carries the malformed attribute id=\"#\" so an id selector is unusable, and #emailVerify .btn-primary is an equally unique fallback) after an address is typed into #verifyEmail (1 match); then 'Verify Code' = #verifyEmailCodeBtn (1 match) after the emailed OTP is typed into #verifyEmailCode (1 match, minlength=5, initially display:none). Clearing stage 2 dismisses #emailVerify and the backdrop and releases form#cfiveForm. ORDERING CAVEAT for the generated flow: this OTP is an ENTRY gate, so the applicant handoff must be satisfied BEFORE any fill step, not at review/submit where captcha/otp handoffs are placed by default.
